dialogues.title: Daily Stand-up
dialogues.about: İki takım arkadaşı günlük toplantıda dünkü işlerini, bugünkü planlarını ve engellerini anlatıyor.

lines.t: Good morning, Tom. Let's start the stand-up.
Morning, Sara. Yesterday I finished the login page and fixed two small bugs.
Great. What are you working on today?
Today I will connect the login page to the API. After that I will write some unit tests.
Do you have any blockers?
Yes, one. I don't have the API key for the test server yet.
OK, I will ask the backend team right now. You should get it before lunch.
Thanks, that would help a lot. What about you?
Yesterday I reviewed three pull requests. Today I will update the documentation and prepare the release notes.
Sounds good. Let's meet again tomorrow at nine.

questions.q: What did Tom finish yesterday?
options: The login page and two bug fixes
questions.why: Tom: 'I finished the login page and fixed two small bugs.'

questions.q: What is Tom's blocker?
options: He has no API key for the test server

questions.q: What will Sara do today?
options: Update the documentation and prepare release notes
questions.why: Sara dokümantasyonu güncelleyip release notes hazırlayacak.

dialogues.title: A Code Review
dialogues.about: Bir geliştirici, takım arkadaşının pull request'ini inceliyor ve önerilerde bulunuyor.

lines.t: Hi Ali, I looked at your pull request. Overall it looks good, but I have a few comments.
Thanks for the quick review. What did you find?
First, the function that calculates the discount is too long. It does three different things.
You're right. Should I split it into smaller functions?
Yes, that would make it easier to read and to test. Also, the variable name 'x' is not very clear.
Good point. I will rename it to 'totalPrice'.
One more thing. I could not find a test for the case when the cart is empty.
Oh, I forgot that edge case. I'll add a unit test for it today.
Perfect. Once you push the changes, I will approve the pull request.
Great, thanks for the helpful feedback.

questions.q: What is the problem with the discount function?
options: It is too long and does several things
questions.why: 'It is too long. It does three different things.'

questions.q: Why does the reviewer mention the variable 'x'?
What test is missing?
options: A test for a large cart
A test for an empty cart
questions.why: Boş sepet (empty cart) için test yok.

questions.q: When will the reviewer approve the pull request?
questions.why: 'Once you push the changes, I will approve...'

dialogues.title: Reporting a Bug
dialogues.about: Bir test uzmanı ve bir geliştirici, uygulamanın çökmesine neden olan hatayı birlikte yeniden üretmeye çalışıyor.

lines.t: Hi Daniel, I found a serious bug in the mobile app. It crashes when I upload a profile photo.
Can you reproduce it every time?
Almost every time. It only happens when the photo is larger than five megabytes.
Interesting. Which phone and which version of the app are you using?
An iPhone 13, version 2.4.1. I attached the crash log to the ticket.
Thanks. I think the problem is the file size limit. The server might reject large files without sending an error message.
That makes sense. The app just freezes and then closes.
I will add a check before the upload and show a friendly message to the user.
Good idea. Can you also give me a workaround for the testers?
Sure. For now, they can use smaller photos. I will fix it in the next patch.

questions.q: When does the app crash?
options: When uploading a photo larger than 5 MB

questions.q: What did the tester attach to the ticket?
questions.why: 'I attached the crash log to the ticket.'

questions.q: What is the workaround for the testers?
questions.why: Geçici çözüm: daha küçük fotoğraf kullanmak.

dialogues.title: A Junior Developer Interview
dialogues.about: Bir şirket, stajyer/junior geliştirici adayıyla projeleri ve güçlü yönleri hakkında konuşuyor.

lines.t: Welcome, Elif. Thank you for coming. Could you tell me a little about yourself?
Thank you for having me. I'm a second-year software engineering student. I enjoy building mobile apps and solving problems.
Can you describe a project you are proud of?
Yes. Last semester I built a mobile app that shows cafeteria menus for universities. It reads the data from a server and updates every day.
That sounds useful. What was the hardest part?
The data from the school was sometimes wrong, so I wrote code to detect and fix mistakes automatically.
How do you work in a team?
I try to communicate clearly. If I'm blocked, I ask for help early. I also like code reviews because I learn a lot from them.
What is one weakness you are working on?
I sometimes spend too much time making code perfect. Now I try to finish a working version first and improve it later.
Thank you, Elif. We will contact you next week.

questions.q: What kind of project did Elif describe?
options: A mobile app for cafeteria menus

questions.q: What was the hardest part of her project?
options: Fixing wrong data from the school

questions.q: What does Elif do when she is blocked?
questions.why: 'If I'm blocked, I ask for help early.'

questions.q: What is her weakness?
options: She spends too much time making code perfect
questions.why: Kodu mükemmel yapmaya fazla zaman harcıyor.

dialogues.title: Help with Git
dialogues.about: Bir stajyer, kıdemli bir arkadaşından dal (branch) ve birleştirme çakışması konusunda yardım istiyor.

lines.t: Excuse me, Mark. Do you have a minute? I have a problem with Git.
Sure, Nina. What's wrong?
I tried to merge my branch into main, but I got a conflict.
Don't worry, conflicts are normal. It means two people changed the same line.
What should I do now?
Open the file. You will see markers that show both versions. Choose the correct code and delete the markers.
And then?
Save the file, add it, and create a new commit. Then push your branch.
That sounds easy. Thank you so much!
No problem. Next time, pull the latest changes before you start working. It helps to avoid conflicts.

questions.q: What problem does Nina have?
What does a conflict mean?
options: Two people changed the same line

questions.q: How can she avoid conflicts next time?
options: Work on the main branch only
Pull the latest changes before she starts
questions.why: Çalışmaya başlamadan önce son değişiklikleri çekmek.

dialogues.title: A Production Incident
dialogues.about: Canlı ortamda bir kesinti yaşanıyor; ekip sorunu bulup önceki sürüme dönüyor ve sonraki adımları konuşuyor.

lines.t: Everyone, we have an incident. The website is returning errors for about thirty percent of the users.
I'm looking at the monitoring dashboard now. The error rate went up right after the last release.
How long ago did we deploy?
About twenty minutes ago. The new version changed how we connect to the database.
Then the safest option is to roll back to the previous version. Do we agree?
Yes. I'll start the rollback right now. It should take around five minutes.
While you do that, I will update the status page and inform the customers.
The rollback is complete. Error rates are dropping. Everything looks normal again.
Great work. Let's write down a timeline of what happened while it is still fresh.
Agreed. Tomorrow we should hold a postmortem and find out why our tests did not catch this problem.
Yes, and we should add an alert for database connection errors so we notice it faster next time.

questions.q: How many users were affected?
What caused the problem?
options: A change in how the app connects to the database

questions.q: What was the decision?
options: Roll back to the previous version

questions.q: What will they do tomorrow?

dialogues.title: Sprint Planning
dialogues.about: Scrum takımı iki haftalık sprint için iş listesinden görev seçiyor ve tahmin yapıyor.

lines.t: Let's start the sprint planning. Our goal for this sprint is to release the new search feature.
I looked at the backlog. The search story has the highest priority.
How long do you think it will take?
I estimate about five days for the backend and three days for the frontend.
That is a lot. Can we reduce the scope?
We could skip the filters for now and add them in the next sprint.
Good idea. Let's focus on a simple version first. What about the bug fixes?
We have two critical bugs. I suggest we fix them first because they affect many users.
Agreed. Then we will have enough time for the search feature and some testing.
Perfect. I will create the tasks and assign them to the team.

questions.q: What is the goal of the sprint?
How do they reduce the scope?
Why do they fix the critical bugs first?

dialogues.title: Clarifying Requirements
dialogues.about: Bir analist müşteriden "hızlı bir uygulama" isteğinin ne anlama geldiğini netleştirmesini istiyor.

lines.t: Thanks for meeting with us. You mentioned that you want the app to be fast. Could you clarify what that means for you?
Well, our users get frustrated when they wait. I want pages to open immediately.
Let's be more specific. Would two seconds be acceptable for the main page?
Two seconds is fine, but the search results must appear in less than one second.
Understood. How many users do you expect at the same time?
Right now about five hundred, but we plan to grow to ten thousand within a year.
In that case, we should design the system to be scalable from the beginning.
Will that make the project more expensive?
Slightly, but it will save money later. Otherwise you would need to rebuild the system when you grow.
That makes sense. Please write these points in the specification so we can approve them.
Of course. I'll send you a draft by Friday.

questions.q: What must happen in less than one second?
questions.why: Arama sonuçları 1 saniyeden kısa sürede gelmeli.

questions.q: How many users does the client expect in a year?
questions.why: Bir yıl içinde on bin kullanıcı.

questions.q: Why does the analyst recommend a scalable design?
questions.why: Sonradan sistemi yeniden yazmak zorunda kalmamak için.

questions.q: When will the analyst send the draft?
questions.why: 'I'll send you a draft by Friday.'

dialogues.title: Pair Programming
dialogues.about: İki geliştirici birlikte çalışarak bir döngüdeki hatayı buluyor.

lines.t: OK, I'm the driver, so I will type. You are the navigator, so you tell me what to think about.
Sounds good. The goal is to find out why the list is empty at the end.
Let me add a breakpoint inside the loop and run the debugger.
Look at the variable 'count'. It is always zero.
You're right. Wait... I see it. We create a new list on every iteration.
Exactly. We should create the list before the loop and only add items inside it.
Let me fix that. Now I run the code again.
It works! The list has twelve items. Let's write a test so this bug cannot come back.
Good idea. Pair programming is really helpful. I would not have seen that alone.

questions.q: What is the bug?
options: A new list is created on every iteration
The variable has the wrong name

questions.q: What does the navigator do?
options: Tells the driver what to think about

questions.q: What do they do after the fix?
questions.why: Hatanın geri gelmemesi için test yazıyorlar.

dialogues.title: First Day at the Company
dialogues.about: Yeni bir çalışan ilk gün iş arkadaşıyla geliştirme ortamını kuruyor.

lines.t: Welcome to the team, Can! I'm Julia. I will help you during your first week.
Thank you, Julia. I'm a little nervous, but I'm excited.
Don't worry. First, let's set up your laptop. You need to install the editor and clone the main repository.
Which version control system do you use?
We use Git. I will give you access to our repository on GitHub.
Great. Where can I find the documentation?
It is in the wiki. Please read the getting started page today.
OK. And when is the team meeting?
Every morning at nine thirty. It's a short stand-up. You can just say what you plan to learn today.
That sounds friendly. Thank you for your help.

questions.q: What must Can install first?
Where is the documentation?
When is the daily team meeting?

dialogues.title: Short Talk: Why We Moved to Microservices
dialogues.about: Tek konuşmacılı kısa bir teknik sunum: bir şirket monolit yapıdan mikroservislere neden geçti?

lines.t: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I want to talk about why our company moved from a monolith to microservices.
Three years ago, our application was one big program. Every team worked in the same code base. It was simple at the beginning, but it became harder every month.
First, a small change required us to deploy the whole application. A tiny bug in one module could bring down everything.
Second, the teams were blocking each other. They had to wait for each other before they could release anything.
So we split the system into small services. Each service has one job, its own database, and its own team.
The result was positive. We now deploy many times a day, and a failure in one service does not stop the others.
However, microservices are not free. We needed better monitoring, and the network between services became a new source of problems.
My advice is simple. Do not start with microservices. Start simple, and split the system only when the pain is real. Thank you for listening.

What is one advantage of microservices mentioned?
options: A failure in one service does not stop the others

questions.q: What is the speaker's advice?
options: Start simple and split only when needed
questions.why: Basit başla, sadece gerçekten gerektiğinde böl.

questions.q: What new problem did microservices create?
questions.why: Servisler arası ağ yeni sorun kaynağı oldu.

dialogues.title: Release on Friday?
dialogues.about: İki mühendis, yeni sürümü cuma günü yayınlamanın riskli olup olmadığını tartışıyor.

lines.t: The new version is ready. I think we should deploy it today.
Today is Friday. I'm not sure that's a good idea.
Why not? All the tests are green.
If something goes wrong, we will have to work during the weekend. And half of the team is already gone.
That's a fair point. But the customers are waiting for this feature.
What if we release on Monday morning instead? Then everyone is here and we can react quickly.
OK, I see your point. A delay of one weekend is not a big risk.
Great. In the meantime, we can test it once more in the staging environment.
Agreed. I'll tell the product manager that we will deploy on Monday.

questions.q: Why is the second speaker against releasing on Friday?
options: They may have to work during the weekend
questions.why: Sorun çıkarsa hafta sonu çalışmak gerekir.

questions.q: When do they decide to release?
What will they do in the meantime?
questions.why: Staging ortamında bir kez daha test.

dialogues.title: Building a Flutter App
dialogues.about: İki geliştirici Flutter uygulamasının ekranını hot reload ile tasarlıyor ve yayına hazırlanıyor.

lines.t: How is the new screen coming along?
Pretty well. I built the layout with a few widgets, and hot reload makes the work really fast.
Nice. Did you test it on a real phone or only on the emulator?
Only on the emulator so far. Tomorrow I will install it on my phone and check the animation.
Good. Remember that the app has to work offline too.
Yes, I save the last data in local storage, so the menu still appears without internet.
Perfect. When do you want to send it to the App Store?
After I fix the crash report from yesterday. I will also increase the build number.
OK. Let me know when it is ready, and I will review the code.

questions.q: Why does the developer like hot reload?
options: It makes the work very fast

questions.q: Where has the screen been tested so far?
How does the app work without internet?
options: It saves the last data in local storage

questions.q: What must be done before sending the app to the App Store?
options: Fix the crash and increase the build number
questions.why: Çökmeyi düzeltmek ve derleme numarasını artırmak.

dialogues.title: A Game Design Review
dialogues.about: Bir oyun tasarımcısı ve bir programcı, koşu oyununun zorluk eğrisini ve oyun testinden gelen geri bildirimi konuşuyor.

lines.t: I watched three friends playtest the runner game yesterday. Most of them lost in the first minute.
That means the difficulty curve is too steep. The first obstacles come too fast.
Exactly. I suggest we spawn fewer enemies at the beginning and add them slowly.
I can do that. I will also make the collider of the spikes a little smaller, because the players say it feels unfair.
Good idea. What about the power-ups?
The magnet power-up is popular. People love it when the coins fly to the character.
Let's add a short cooldown to the skill, so it does not become too strong.
Agreed. After that, I will check the frame rate on an old phone.
Great. Let's playtest again on Friday.

questions.q: What was the problem in the playtest?
options: Most players lost in the first minute

questions.q: How will they fix the difficulty curve?
options: Spawn fewer enemies at the beginning

questions.q: Why will the programmer make the spike collider smaller?
options: It is a bug in the engine

questions.q: What will they check on an old phone?

dialogues.title: Using AI Tools Wisely
dialogues.about: Bir mentor ve bir stajyer, yapay zeka araçlarını kod yazarken nasıl güvenle kullanacaklarını konuşuyor.

lines.t: I noticed you used an AI assistant to write the function. How did it go?
It was fast, but the first answer had a hallucination. It used a method that does not exist.
That happens often. The important part is that you checked the result instead of trusting it.
I ran the tests, and they failed. Then I read the documentation and fixed the code myself.
Exactly. Treat the assistant like a fast but sometimes careless colleague.
Should I tell the team when I use it?
Yes. Be open about it, and never paste private data or passwords into a prompt.
That makes sense. I also want to understand every line I submit, not just copy it.
That is the right attitude. If you cannot explain the code, you do not own it yet.
I will remember that. Thank you for the advice.

options: It used a method that does not exist

questions.q: How did the intern find the problem?
